page.overview:
What is Final Fantasy worlds?

The Final Fantasy games take place in various worlds. Each new installment usually takes place in a new world and universe, although there are some exceptions. Ivalice is a Final Fantasy world visited in numerous games that could be considered to form their own sub-series, but the Ivalice in each game is vastly different, akin to having a whole new world for every game. Final Fantasy worlds are self-contained, but could be considered loosely part of a multiverse connected through the interdimensional rift, a dimension of between realms which transcends time and space.

The original Final Fantasy was heavily influenced by Dungeons & Dragons and thus its world is similar to a typical fantasy world in the tabletop game. However, Final Fantasy worlds since have had various design philosophies and settings, which grew more diverse once the series reached 3D, from the contemporary fantasy, pre-2000 world of Final Fantasy VIII, to the futuristic floating world of Cocoon flying over its wild sister world of Gran Pulse in Final Fantasy XIII.

Recurring features among the worlds featured in Final Fantasy include crystals which often have major influence in the world or are associated with magic, ancient civilizations with advanced technology, and races and creatures such as moogles and chocobos.

Final Fantasy takes place in an unnamed fantasy world with three large continents. Though never named in the original game, a world loosely based on it referred to as "World A" in Dissidia 012 Final Fantasy. In Stranger of Paradise Final Fantasy Origin, the area of the world based on the original Final Fantasy is called "Cornelia".
